Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

extreme adjective

the greatest or the farthest: utmost, outermost

also utmost, outermost, extremes, in the extreme, a last resort, farthest

classical

Cic. Off. 1.33: summum jūs summa injūria
Cic. Rep. 1.1: ad summam senectūtem, to extreme old age (Lewis & Short)

summus, summa, summum

adjective, superlative of superus, declension

utmost, greatest (in degree)

The utmost degree of a thing: the greatest danger, extreme old age, summā vōce, at the top of one’s voice. Its first sense is the top of a thing (summus mōns, the mountain top).

Other words

  • extrēmus, extrēma, extrēmum — outermost, farthest, last; extreme

    adjective, superlative of exter, declension · classical · Caes. B.G. 3.3.4: ad extrēmum cāsum; Catull. 11.2: in extrēmōs … Indōs

    At the far edge or the end: the farthest borders, the last day (Lewis & Short: “the outermost, utmost, extreme, so most freq.”); and so the last resort, the extreme case. Lewis & Short notes that extrēmus is not compared in classical Latin.

  • ultimus, ultima, ultimum — farthest, last

    adjective, superlative of ulterior, declension · also used · classical · Caes. B.G. 6.29.3: partem ultimam pontis

    The farthest away, or the last in a series; less often of degree than summus.

Examples

  • summum jūs summa injūria

    extreme justice is extreme injusticeCic. Off. 1.33

  • Majōrī tamen partī placuit, hōc reservātō ad extrēmum cāsum cōnsiliō interim reī ēventum experīrī et castra dēfendere.

    But most of them decided to keep this plan as a last resort, and meanwhile to wait and see how things turned out and defend the camp.Caes. B.G. 3.3.4

  • sīve in extrēmōs penetrābit Indōs … sīve trāns altās gradiētur Alpēs

    whether he will make his way to the farthest Indians … or march across the high AlpsCatull. 11.2, 9

See also maximum, most, limit, far.
